title: elasticity-sensitivity-study-rolling-window-oct-2024
content:
Purpose:
Capture raw experiment runs for rolling-window based elasticity tests against production-ish traffic (staging mirrored) to tune min/max, scale triggers, and cooldowns across region-specific GPU pools. This sheet contains per-run inputs, observed signals, short notes and recommended follow-ups. Rough working doc — expect shorthand and TODOs.

Table (each line = row):
Date | Region | GPU Pool | MinReplicas | MaxReplicas | ScaleUpTrigger(util%) | ScaleDownTrigger(util%) | RollingWindowSec | CooldownSec | ObservedP95Latency(ms) | ObservedUtilAvg(%) | TriggeredActions | Notes | Outcome
2024-10-15 | us-west1 | general-gpu-v2 | 2 | 12 | 78 | 45 | 300 | 120 | 210 | 61 | scale_up @ +3 pods | saw brief oscillation after burst, prewarm cache missing | unstable - needs hysteresis
2024-10-16 | us-east1 | highmem-gpu | 1 | 8 | 72 | 40 | 180 | 90 | 180 | 54 | no action | low sustained traffic, underutilized; unexplained small spikes correlating with nightly batch | OK but overprovisioned at min=1
2024-10-18 | eu-west1 | general-gpu-v2 | 3 | 16 | 80 | 50 | 600 | 180 | 260 | 68 | scale_up then scale_down | long rolling window prevented quick recovery causing latency tail | conservative window hurts SLA
2024-10-20 | ap-south1 | burst-pool | 0 | 6 | 85 | 35 | 120 | 60 | 240 | 73 | scale_up (burst) | burst pool responded fine but cooldown too short -> repeated flapping | increase cooldown / add min=1 for business-critical routes
2024-10-22 | us-west1 | general-gpu-v2 | 2 | 12 | 75 | 50 | 240 | 300 | 230 | 63 | no action | long cooldown (300s) suppressed scaling back -> higher cost but stable latency | cost stable, latency good
2024-10-25 | eu-west1 | quantized-pool | 1 | 10 | 70 | 38 | 240 | 120 | 200 | 59 | rapid scale_up | quantized models show higher util due to CPU overhead on host, triggered more often | need different trigger for quantized pool
2024-10-27 | us-east1 | general-gpu-v2 | 2 | 12 | 82 | 55 | 120 | 120 | 195 | 66 | scale_up once | higher up-threshold prevented unnecessary scale for small bursts, latency contained | promising (raise up-threshold for noisy regions)

Interpretation notes (working):
- RollingWindowSec tradeoffs: shorter windows (120s) pick up bursts quickly but cause flapping on noisy signal; longer windows (600s) smooth noise but delay reaction and increase tail latency. For low-latency routes prefer 120-240s, for batch-heavy prefer 600s.
- Up-threshold: 80% is a reasonable baseline for general pools; high-variance regions (ap-south1) should use higher up-threshold (85%) or dedicated burst pool.
- Down-threshold: set aggressively lower (35-45%) for burst pools to allow fast reclaim; for general pools 45-55% reduces churn.
- Cooldown: short cooldowns (<120s) often cause oscillation in pools with cold-start cost. Increase cooldown to 180-300s where model cold-start penalty > 150ms.
- Min replicas: having min=0 for burst pools saves cost but increases tail latency on first requests. For customer-facing routes set min>=1.
- Quantized pools behave differently; CPU-bound pre/post-processing can raise util. Use a separate trigger profile for quantized-pool.

Action items (assigned):
- Asha: run tensor/serve warmup experiment with min=1 on ap-south1 burst pool and measure P99 (due 2024-11-08). Linked: JIRA-OPS-1428.
- Marcus: implement hysteresis (require sustained over-threshold for 2 consecutive windows) in autoscaler prototype and run A/B in us-west1 (due 2024-11-12).
- Ravi: produce rollout plan to adjust default profiles: general pools -> up=80/down=45/window=240/cooldown=180; burst pools -> up=85/down=35/window=120/cooldown=120 (draft 2024-11-05).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we incorporate KV-cache hit metrics into the trigger (reduce scale-ups when cache-hit high)? (investigate instrumentation; ticket created)
- Should region-specific costs (spot availability, egress) factor into routing policy instead of relying solely on per-pool triggers?
- Need a cost simulation to estimate monthly $ impact for each profile change (ask finance for quick model).

Quick summary for execs (1-2 lines):
We tested rolling-window elasticity across 7 config variants in staging traffic. Best practical tradeoff: up-threshold ~80%, window 120-240s, cooldown 180s for general pools and stricter thresholds for noisy/bursty regions. Next steps: implement hysteresis, run warmup for burst pools, and create cost delta sim.

Raw CSV export available on request from the autoscaler test harness (run id -> see linked PR).

Notes to reviewer: this is a working sheet — if you copy into a spreadsheet, columns are pipe-separated with header on top. Add comments inline if you run new experiment and update last_modified.
